trust_decision.summary: Whether a request may open the HUD websocket / read HUD state is decided in the upgrader's CheckOrigin (csrf query param OR same-origin fallback that passes when Origin is absent), and the HUD HTTP routes, including the csrf-token issuer /api/websocket_token, have no session-token check at all.

landing_point.why: The summary names cross-site WebSocket hijacking of the HUD stream; the upgrader's CheckOrigin with its origin fallback is the obvious first stop.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The CLI 'tilt logs' dials /ws/view with no csrf param and no Origin header, relying on the origin fallback; 'tilt dump'/'tilt trigger' call HUD routes with no token; the web HUD fetches /api/websocket_token with the cookie then opens the socket with ?csrf=. A fix that drops the fallback or gates routes without updating clients breaks these. The published fix itself did not update tilt logs; upstream later added a csrf fetch (latest/internal/hud/client/log_streamer.go:41).
